primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Chondroblastoma is a benign primary bone tumor composed of immature chondroblasts, typically arising in the epiphysis of long bones in adolescents and young adults. Histology shows polygonal chondroblasts, osteoclast-type giant cells, chondroid matrix, and characteristic fine pericellular 'chicken-wire' calcification.
vignette: A 16-year-old boy has 7 months of gradually worsening pain around the right knee. Radiographs show a well-circumscribed lytic lesion with a thin sclerotic rim centered in the epiphysis of the distal femur. There is no periosteal reaction or soft-tissue mass.
lead: Which histologic finding is most characteristic of this lesion?
correct: Polygonal chondroblasts with scattered giant cells and fine pericellular 'chicken-wire' calcification
distractors: Uniform giant cells diffusely distributed among mononuclear stromal cells without a chondroid matrix
Interlacing trabeculae of woven bone rimmed by osteoblasts within a vascular stroma
Lobules of hypocellular myxoid and chondroid tissue separated by fibrous septa
Sheets of malignant osteoblasts producing lace-like osteoid with marked cytologic atypia
distractor_notes: This describes giant cell tumor of bone, which more often occurs after skeletal maturity and shows diffusely distributed osteoclast-like giant cells without the characteristic chondroblastoma chicken-wire calcification.
This pattern is typical of osteoid osteoma/osteoblastoma, which are osteoid-producing tumors rather than epiphyseal chondroblastic tumors.
This is characteristic of chondromyxoid fibroma, usually a metaphyseal eccentric lesion with lobulated myxoid/chondroid histology.
Malignant osteoid production is diagnostic of osteosarcoma and would not fit the small well-circumscribed epiphyseal lesion shown.
key_expl: An epiphyseal lytic lesion in an adolescent strongly suggests chondroblastoma. Histology typically contains sheets of round or polygonal chondroblasts with grooved nuclei, scattered osteoclast-type giant cells, focal chondroid material, and delicate pericellular calcification that produces the classic 'chicken-wire' pattern. The epiphyseal location and this calcification distinguish chondroblastoma from other giant-cell-containing and cartilage-forming bone tumors.
objective: Recognize chondroblastoma by its adolescent epiphyseal location and characteristic chondroblast/giant-cell histology with pericellular chicken-wire calcification.
